item.title: Savor: Fresh Starts: How California Farmers Markets Changed the Way We Eat — Wed Oct 28, 5:00 PM — Robert Mondavi Institute - Sensory Building
item.description:
Join us for this quarter's Savor event: Fresh Starts: How California Farmers Markets Changed the Way We Eat.
The formation of the Davis Farmers Market 50 years ago was a revolutionary movement to connect consumers directly to farmers and helped shape the fresh flavors of California cuisine. Markets have been a cornerstone of the community and have also played a pivotal role in food access, especially during supply chain shortages and widespread food recalls. Inevitably, markets have evolved. Join us as we explore the history, impact and changing role of farmers markets in local communities.
The event will feature a panel of leading industry experts including:
Ann Evans, UC Davis alumna, co-founder of the Davis Farmers Market and Davis Food Co-op, author and former mayor and city council member of the City of DavisSam Greenlee, chief executive officer of Alchemist Community Development CorporationChutharat Sae Tong, co-owner of Majka Pizzeria and Bakery in SacramentoModerator Ca

item.title: Manetti Shrem Museum: Together Again, 1960–2026, Perspectives from UC Davis’ Fine Arts Collection — Thu Oct 29, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description: Together Again inaugurates the Manetti Shrem Museum’s ongoing collection galleries. This exhibition highlighting the collection will be on long-term view, accompanied by temporary exhibitions each fall and winter. The ongoing collection galleries trace a history of art forged from UC Davis and throughout Northern California. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, this presentation proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri. Together Again builds bridges between who we were and who we are becoming at UC Davis, and affirms the Manetti Shrem Museum as home to the complex story of No

item.title: Out of Line: Art at the Edge — Thu Oct 29, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
Inspired by conceptual artist Bruce Nauman’s video work “Dance or Exercise on the Perimeter of a Square (Square Dance), 1967–68,” this exhibition explores Davis as a site of both artistic practice and political protest. Mike Henderson, Ester Hernandez, Malaquías Montoya, Bruce Nauman, Nancy Rubins, Dorothy Wiley and the student artists of UC Davis’ Third World Forum engage with film, print and performance to confront who they were and what their work meant in a world of radical change. They made work wherever and however they could: in collaborative workshops, student newsrooms, kitchens and living rooms. While rooted in the politics of the late 20th century, “Out of Line” finds renewed meaning in the present day.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Dia de los Muertos Public Altar — Thu Oct 29, 3:00 PM — Davis Cemetery
item.description: On an annual basis, the Davis Cemetery District hosts a Dia de los Muertos (Day of the Dead) celebration on our grounds. This celebration is one of the last Mesoamerican indigenous influenced rituals, honoring mother earth and all ancestors. This celebration is part of an effort to create a community, a sense of belonging, and global awareness of cultural richness in our multicultural society. The Davis Cemetery District’s annual Día de los Muertos public altar was set up on Thursday, October 29th and will remain in place through November 2nd. In addition to the public ofrenda, we will offer grave cleaning supplies, and educational signage highlighting the traditions and significance of Día de los Muertos. This year will also feature a designated pathway decorated with marigolds and papel picado, encouraging visitors to stroll through the cemetery, reflect, and honor the memories of their loved ones. item.title: Galactic Featuring Jelly Joseph With special guest Bella Rayne Band — Thu Oct 29, 7:30 PM — Mondavi Center (Mondavi) UC Davis Campus
item.description:
For more than 30 years, Galactic has been a powerhouse of New Orleans music, fusing funk, jazz, rock, hip-hop and soul into a sound unmistakably their own. The group has evolved from a late-night funk outfit into a genre-defying collective known for their electrifying live performances and adventurous collaborations. Joined by dynamic lead vocalist Anjelika “Jelly” Joseph, Galactic brings a fresh energy to Mondavi Center’s Jackson Hall, with Joseph’s soulful, commanding voice adding a powerful dimension to the band’s expansive sound. Opener Bella Rayne, a vocalist and songwriter, and her guitar-driven ensemble, blend Americana and the improvisational spirit of the jam-band tradition.
Source: The Dirt

Tim McNary is a Cinematic Folk Artist from the Southern United States. He found his passion for songwriting while backpacking throughout South America after college. The Nashville based songwriter traverses emotional and geographical borders with multi-dimensional songwriting and evocative vocals. Some of his musical influences include Ben Howard, Foy Vance, & Leif Vollebekk. He’s had dozens of film & tv placements, collaborated with a host of recognized songwriters, and toured extensively around the United States & Canada. $20 General Admission $15 Students (in-store or at the door only, w/ID) $15 Kids under 12 (in-store or at the door only) Doors open at 7:00pm This is a BYOB event!

item.title: Light & Grain — Fri Oct 30 — The Artery
item.description:
The Artery presents “Light & Grain,” a two-person exhibition featuring oil painter Kristina Kernytska and woodworker Viktor Ivantsov. The exhibition runs October 30 through November 23, with an artists’ reception on Friday, November 13, from 6–9 p.m., coinciding with the Davis Second Friday ArtAbout. “Light & Grain” brings together two distinct approaches to natural beauty: the raw, carved grain of wood and the vibrant, textured light of oil paint. Kristina Kernytska’s paintings and Viktor Ivantsov’s wood carvings invite viewers to experience nature through texture, memory, and light. Together, the works celebrate the landscapes and living world that inspire both artists.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Birds & Bikes — Fri Oct 30, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: Axis Gallery is proud to announce Birds & Bikes, a collaborative art exhibition bringing together regional artists to explore the poetic intersections of avian flight and human motion. Running from October 2 through November 1, 2026, the exhibition showcases a dynamic range of works from intricate metal sculptures and imaginative textile art to curated gallery shop goods, celebrating the beauty of migration alongside the engineering of daily travel. The exhibition features a direct partnership with the City of Sacramento Office of Arts and Culture (OAC) Art in Public Places program and North Natomas Jibe. Birds & Bikes serves as an artistic tie-in to the upcoming Birds and Benches project, which will install artist-designed public benches across North Natomas Regional Park. Visitors are invited to experience the unique ecology and transit identity of the Natomas Basin through a collaborative lens, discover one-of-a-kind art pieces, and browse handcrafted items in the East Gallery Pop

item.title: Portraits of Things: Paintings by Gioia Fonda and Charlie Gill — Fri Nov 6, 11:30 AM — Pence Gallery
item.description:
Portraits of Things: Paintings by Gioia Fonda and Charlie Gill at Pence Gallery in Davis Exhibit: October 9 – November 29, 2026 Reception: Friday, October 9, 6-9 PM (Free) Artist Talk: Sunday, November 8, 2-3:30 PM (Free)
Interdisciplinary artist Gioia Fonda has long collected colorful toys, both for their intrinsic charm and as creative inspiration. As a student at California College of the Arts, she arranged small collectibles into still-life compositions, captured them on film, and processed the photos at a local drugstore. Captivated by these arrangements, her advisor, Charlie Gill, painted spare compositions based on her photographs—works that now hang alongside hers. For this exhibition, Fonda has created a series of new paintings featuring similar arrangements of toys and found objects. She is also offering an opportunity for members of the public to exhibit their own small works on paper, riffing on some of her recent photos. Artists may add to this display throughout th

item.title: Davis Musical Theatre Presents Mean Girls — Fri Nov 6, 7:30 PM — Davis Musical Theatre Company (DMTC)
item.description:
Davis Musical Theatre Presents Mean Girls Cady Heron may have grown up on an African savanna, but nothing prepared her for the wild and vicious ways of her strange new home: suburban Illinois. When Cady encounters The Plastics—a trio of powerful frenemies led by the charming but ruthless Regina George—she becomes caught in the school’s popularity hierarchy. Cady and her new friends devise a “Revenge Party” to end Regina’s reign, but Cady soon learns that taking down a queen bee can come at a cost—and that losing yourself is far more dangerous than losing a popularity contest. *Mean Girls contains mature themes and language*
Source: Visit Yolo

item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. item.title: Diwali, Festival of Lights — Sun Nov 8 — CA
item.description:
Diwali is celebrated by many Hindus, Jains, Sikhs, and some Buddhists, with traditions that vary across communities. Often associated with light, hope, renewal, and the triumph of good over evil, the festival brings families and communities together. Learning about Diwali is one way to celebrate religious diversity and build understanding across cultures. Learn more here.

item.title: Portraits of Things: Paintings by Gioia Fonda and Charlie Gill — Thu Oct 29, 11:30 AM — Pence Gallery
item.description:
Portraits of Things: Paintings by Gioia Fonda and Charlie Gill at Pence Gallery in Davis Exhibit: October 9 – November 29, 2026 Reception: Friday, October 9, 6-9 PM (Free) Artist Talk: Sunday, November 8, 2-3:30 PM (Free)
Interdisciplinary artist Gioia Fonda has long collected colorful toys, both for their intrinsic charm and as creative inspiration. As a student at California College of the Arts, she arranged small collectibles into still-life compositions, captured them on film, and processed the photos at a local drugstore. Captivated by these arrangements, her advisor, Charlie Gill, painted spare compositions based on her photographs—works that now hang alongside hers. For this exhibition, Fonda has created a series of new paintings featuring similar arrangements of toys and found objects. She is also offering an opportunity for members of the public to exhibit their own small works on paper, riffing on some of her recent photos. Artists may add to this display throughout th

item.title: Bohème Bewitched — Thu Oct 29, 3:00 PM — Bohème Bewitched
item.description:
An enchanted interactive experience from Bohème in Davis, the thrift boutique two blocks away. Quests through a glowing grove, a blacklight zombie forest, a frog bog, a mermaid lagoon, a witch’s cottage and a wood full of wisps. Spooky, not scary. Six enchanted lands inside the old bank at 300 E Street, downtown Davis: the old Union Bank building at the corner of 3rd and E, next to Panera Bread, one block from Central Park. Hours: Wednesday to Friday 3:00 to 6:30pm. Saturday and Sunday 11:00am to 6:30pm. Closed Mondays and Tuesdays. Open 11am to 6:30pm on Saturday, October 31. $4 at the door for the experience, credited to any $8 purchase in the shop (same visit only). Open to all ages every day until 6:30pm. Enchanted Evenings: special evening events run 7 to 9:30pm on Oct 23, 24 and 30. $13 online, $15 at the door. Every date, hours and tickets: bohemebewitched.com
Source: Visit Yolo

item.title: Tim McNary Live @ The Melon Ball — Thu Oct 29, 7:30 PM — The Melon Ball – Watermelon Music
item.description:
Tim McNary Live @ The Melon Ball in Davis Tim McNary is a Cinematic Folk Artist from the Southern United States. He found his passion for songwriting while backpacking throughout South America after college. The Nashville based songwriter traverses emotional and geographical borders with multi-dimensional songwriting and evocative vocals. Some of his musical influences include Ben Howard, Foy Vance, & Leif Vollebekk. He’s had dozens of film & tv placements, collaborated with a host of recognized songwriters, and toured extensively around the United States & Canada. Portraits of Things: Paintings by Gioia Fonda and Charlie Gill at Pence Gallery in Davis Exhibit: October 9 – November 29, 2026 Reception: Friday, October 9, 6-9 PM (Free) Artist Talk: Sunday, November 8, 2-3:30 PM (Free)
Interdisciplinary artist Gioia Fonda has long collected colorful toys, both for their intrinsic charm and as creative inspiration. As a student at California College of the Arts, she arranged small collectibles into still-life compositions, captured them on film, and processed the photos at a local drugstore. Captivated by these arrangements, her advisor, Charlie Gill, painted spare compositions based on her photographs—works that now hang alongside hers. For this exhibition, Fonda has created a series of new paintings featuring similar arrangements of toys and found objects. item.title: Bohème Bewitched — Fri Oct 30, 3:00 PM — Bohème Bewitched
item.description:
An enchanted interactive experience from Bohème in Davis, the thrift boutique two blocks away. Quests through a glowing grove, a blacklight zombie forest, a frog bog, a mermaid lagoon, a witch’s cottage and a wood full of wisps. Spooky, not scary. Six enchanted lands inside the old bank at 300 E Street, downtown Davis: the old Union Bank building at the corner of 3rd and E, next to Panera Bread, one block from Central Park. Hours: Wednesday to Friday 3:00 to 6:30pm. Saturday and Sunday 11:00am to 6:30pm. Closed Mondays and Tuesdays. Open 11am to 6:30pm on Saturday, October 31. $4 at the door for the experience, credited to any $8 purchase in the shop (same visit only). Open to all ages every day until 6:30pm. Enchanted Evenings: special evening events run 7 to 9:30pm on Oct 23, 24 and 30. $13 online, $15 at the door. Every date, hours and tickets: bohemebewitched.com
Source: Visit Yolo

item.title: Mariachi Bonitas Live at The HIVE — Fri Oct 30, 5:30 PM — The HIVE / Z Specialty Food
item.description:
Live at The HIVE presents Mariachi Bonitas during an outdoor concert. Doors at 5:30pm; Music at 6:30pm. Changing the narrative of mariachi in Sacramento and beyond, Mariachi Bonitas de Dinorah Klingler is redefining what it means to be mariachi. Enjoy a seasonal menu, craft beverages and complimentary honey tasting at northern California’s largest honey and mead tasting room. Pay what you can cover charge: $0-$20/person. Family and dog friendly. All ages welcome. No outside food or drinks.
Source: Visit Yolo

item.title: SSRI R&B Jazz Quintet Live @ The Melon Ball — Fri Oct 30, 7:30 PM — The Melon Ball – Watermelon Music
item.description:
Live Music @ The Melon Ball in Davis SSRI is a modern jazz collective that is deeply influenced by artists and groups such as: Robert Glasper, Roy Hargrove, and Lettuce. They perform a diverse repertoire of original contemporary jazz arrangements, standards from The American Song Book, and covers of beloved R&B songs from the 90s and mid 2000s. Each band member has a different musical background, but we’ve drawn together due to our shared love of Jazz, R&B, Gospel and Pop music. Join us as we celebrate the music of Michael Jackson, Luther Vandross, Stevie Wonder, and more! $20 General Admission $15 Seniors/Students $10 Kids under 12 Doors open at 7:00pm Cash or Venmo at the door only (no Credit Card) This is a BYOB event!
Source: Visit Davis, Visit Yolo

item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Sat Oct 31, 8:00 AM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients.
Source: Visit Davis, Visit Yolo

item.title: Together Church: Fall Fest — Sat Oct 31, 5:00 PM — Together Church
item.description:
Together Church invites families to their annual Fall Fest on October 31 from 5:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. at 1541 Merkley Avenue, West Sacramento, CA 95691. This free community event offers an evening of family-friendly fun, including candy, games, activities, and snacks. Admission is free, and everyone is welcome to participate.
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: Sip Yolo with Yolo County Wines — Sat Oct 31, 11:00 AM — Yolo County Vineyard and Winery Association
item.description:
Discover the charm of Yolo County’s wine country this season by visiting our Yolo Wines wineries. From cozy tasting rooms to stunning vineyard views, each tasting room offers award-winning wines, hometown hospitality, and wines perfect for gifting. Gather your friends, sip something new, and make this season a little more delicious.
